text.text_excerpt: If you can get a room here, this is the best deal in the French Quarter, hands down. A little boutique hotel in a historic building, this place has all the charm that you'd expect from New Orleans, with none of the outrageousness of Bourbon Street, which I consider to be a good thing. I stayed in room 202, which has it's own private balcony looking out over Royal Street. It's not nearly as crowded as staying on Bourbon Street, but it's still good people watching. It's located down the street from a Community Coffee shop, which I LOVE, as well as around the corner from Bourbon Street and the French Market and all the historic sights. My girlfriend and I stayed here for our last night in NOLA and we're so happy we did. The hospitality here was refreshing. It feels like you've stepped back into time while staying here. The hotel itself is very old and historic, the grounds date back to the 1700's! It is a little haunted, so if you're into that stuff than you should definitely stay here. And if you're not into that, well i'm sorry but majority of New Orleans is haunted. Loved staying here, affordable prices for a Monday night, a HUGE queen size bed, and a very lovely complimentary breakfast that was delivered to my room. Next time I come back to the big easy I will definitely be staying here!

We were passing through and wanted to try a "haunted" hotel in the French Quarter. We had heard about this hotel in one of the ghost tours a few years ago. I was surprised to read the poor reviews, but think they must have been written before renovations. We were in Room 105. It opened out into the courtyard. This is a historical hotel. We did not expect things to be new and perfect. The room was small, but not cramped. There were iron beds that were not antique. The mattresses were pillow-top and very comfortable.
